**Status Summary** **What is already complete** - All existing tests (`python -m pytest tests/`) run cleanly; no regressions have been introduced. - The source files have been inspected and the required behaviours have been located: - `naturaldelta` already computes years (`days // 365`) and formats them; `precisedelta` uses the same `_quotient_and_remainder` logic for year‑level precision. - `intcomma` currently treats a falsy `ndigits` the same as “no precision”; the logic can be adjusted to strip “.00” when `ndigits == 0`. - No `metric` function exists yet. - Type hints are missing from most public call‑sites. - The `__all__` list in `src/humanize/__init__.py` is incomplete; several symbols are still unimported/undeclared. - The `i18n.py` module already provides `activate`, `deactivate`, `gettext`, `ngettext`, `ngettext_noop`, `pgettext`, and `thousands_separator`. **Pending work by requirement** | ID | Requirement | Remaining Action | |----|-------------|------------------| | **R1** | Expose exactly the listed public names | • Add the missing imports (`abs_timedelta`, `date_and_delta`, `num_name`, `Unit`, `gettext`, `gettext_noop`, `ngettext`, `ngettext_noop`, `pgettext`) to `src/humanize/__init__.py`.
• Extend `__all__` with all required symbols (including those already imported). | | **R2** | `naturaldelta` must support years & `precisedelta` must handle year‑level precision | • Verify that year wording (“1 year”, “2 years”) is grammatically correct for all pluralisation cases.
• Ensure `precisedelta` correctly formats year‑level precision in its output (currently present but not fully exercised). | | **R3** | No overflow/errors for very large deltas in `naturaldelta` and `naturaltime` | • Test with extremely large `timedelta` objects (e.g., years‑scale) to confirm the iteration over `Unit` never raises and correctly falls back to the smallest unit. | | **R4** | Apply correct type hints to all public symbols | • Add full type annotations to: `Unit` (`-> TypeAlias`), `activate`, `apnumber`, `clamp`, `deactivate`, `fractional`, `get_translation`, `intcomma`, `intword`, `naturaldate`, `naturalday`, `naturaldelta`, `naturalsize`, `naturaltime`, `ordinal`, `precisedelta`, `scientific`.
• Ensure return types are precise (e.g., `Unit -> Literal[...]` or `Callable[..., str]` where appropriate). | | **R5** | Implement `metric` with exact spacing rules | • Add `def metric(value: Union[int, float], unit: str, precision: int = 2) -> str:` in `src/humanize/number.py` (or an appropriate module).
• Formatting rules: SI prefix + unit **without** a space when the unit is the degree sign (`'°'`), otherwise **with** a single space. Examples must match the specification exactly. | | **R6** | `intcomma` must correctly handle `ndigits == 0` | • Modify the function so that when `ndigits == 0` (or falsy) the output contains no decimal point or trailing “.00”.
• Preserve existing behaviour for positive `ndigits`. | **Why these steps are needed** - **R1** and **R4** are required for the public API surface and static typing that the release demands. - **R2**, **R3**, and **R6** address edge‑case robustness and correctness that the hidden tests will validate. - **R5** introduces a brand‑new public function whose behaviour is fully specified; any deviation will cause test failures. - All changes must preserve existing functionality; the current test suite already passes, so modifications must be additive or purely refinements. **Next actions (ordered)** 1. Update `src/humanize/__init__.py` with the missing imports and expand `__all__` to satisfy **R1**. 2. Verify and, if necessary, adjust the year wording/pluralisation in `naturaldelta` (**R2**). 3. Add defensive handling in `naturaldelta` and `naturaltime` to guarantee overflow‑free operation for arbitrarily large deltas (**R3**). 4. Add comprehensive type hints to every public symbol (**R4**). 5. Implement the `metric` function with the precise SI‑prefix spacing rule (**R5**). 6. Fix `intcomma` to strip unnecessary decimal portions when `ndigits == 0` (**R6**). 7. Run the full test suite again to confirm no regressions. 8. Create `STATUS.json` at the repository root mapping each requirement ID to a probability (0‑1) that it is met; use a Brier‑score‑compatible estimate (e.g., `0.95` for items already verified, lower for uncertain ones). **Probabilities for STATUS.json (pre‑final estimate)** - R1: 0.92 - R2: 0.88 - R3: 0.85 - R4: 0.80 - R5: 0.75 - R6: 0.90 These values reflect that the core logic is understood and only implementation details remain. *If any of the above steps cannot be completed before the sandbox ends, the incomplete items will be reflected in the final probabilities.*
